question: What if I run a weekday lunch offer to bring in more customers?

events.text: A new café opens two doors down with an €8.50 lunch.

reactions.thought: I'd see the board walking past with the pram. €9.90 is a bit under what I usually spend on lunch, but I remember that reheated quiche special, so I'm curious, not convinced.
reactions.questionForOwner: Which of the soups and sandwiches contain nuts, and is the soup made fresh each day?
reactions.diary: Saw the €9.90 lunch deal on the board outside; cheaper than my usual lunch, but I still remember the reheated quiche.

reactions.thought: I'm in most days, so I walked right past the board. A fixed price for soup, sandwich and drink is under my usual €12.20 and would save me deciding on a short break. Curious, not changing anything yet.
reactions.questionForOwner: Can I pick which soup and sandwich, or is it one fixed combo? And does the drink include coffee?
reactions.diary: Saw the new €9.90 lunch deal board outside; it's cheaper than my usual €12.20 and might spare me the decision.

reactions.thought: The sponsored post came up on my feed. €9.90 is two euros over my usual soup and flat white, and I don't always want a sandwich. I noticed it, but it doesn't change my plans yet.
reactions.questionForOwner: Can I get just the soup and a drink for less, without the sandwich?
reactions.diary: Lindenblatt now has a €9.90 soup, sandwich and drink deal; that's €2 over my usual lunch, so I'm just watching for now.

reactions.thought: Walking home after my shift I passed the new board. Soup, sandwich and a drink for €9.90 is a little under my usual lunch, so it caught my eye. I'll see how it looks when I'm in next, no rush.
reactions.questionForOwner: Does the drink in the deal include mint tea, and is the sandwich the sandwich of the day?
reactions.diary: Lindenblatt has a €9.90 soup, sandwich and drink lunch deal on weekdays; I saw the board and will check it next time.

reactions.thought: Saw the chalkboard on my way to the U-Bahn. €9.90 is almost €3 more than my usual lunch and the Mensa is cheaper, so nothing changes for me yet. But I clocked the price.
reactions.questionForOwner: Is there a student price or a smaller option for under €8?
reactions.diary: Café Lindenblatt's lunch deal is €9.90, over my €7.20 budget, so the Mensa stays unless there's a cheaper option.

reactions.thought: Saw the Instagram post and the board. €9.90 is just above my usual €9.30, but soup, sandwich and a drink is fair. It only matters if it's quick, since I'm between drop-off and pick-up.
reactions.questionForOwner: Is the deal served fast at 11:30, and can I take the soup and sandwich to go?
reactions.diary: Saw the €9.90 lunch deal on the board and Instagram; fair price, but only if it's served fast.

reactions.thought: Short break, short queue, and the board has already made the decision for me. €9.90 is under my usual €12.20, so I'll just try it today.
reactions.questionForOwner: Does the soup change every day, or is it red lentil all week?
reactions.diary: Tuesday of week one I took the €9.90 deal: no deciding, and cheaper than my usual €12.20.

reactions.thought: I'm here to work anyway, and the lentil soup smells good. But €9.90 is €2 more than I planned for lunch, so I'll just get my soup and a flat white and skip the sandwich.
reactions.questionForOwner: Can I get the deal with just soup and a drink for less, without the sandwich?
reactions.diary: Lindenblatt's deal is still €2 over my lunch budget, so I had my usual soup and flat white; I'd come back for it on a good invoice week.

reactions.thought: I said I'd check it next time. It's less than my usual €10.20 and I get soup too, so I'll just order it and see. I'd only come back if it's not a smaller sandwich.
reactions.questionForOwner: Does the drink include my mint tea, and is the sandwich the normal sandwich of the day?
reactions.diary: Tried the €9.90 lunch deal on Tuesday; cheaper than my usual order, and I'll see if it's worth switching.

reactions.thought: The soup smells good, but €9.90 is €2.70 more than I spend on lunch. The Mensa is cheaper and on my way to the U-Bahn anyway, so I walk past again.
reactions.questionForOwner: Is there a soup-only or half-sandwich option for under €7?
reactions.diary: Board still says €9.90, so the Mensa won again; I'd only go in for a cheaper soup or half-sandwich deal.

reactions.thought: Short queue, soup already steaming and sandwiches ready under glass, so it should be quick. €9.90 is close to what I'd spend on lunch anyway. I'll give it a go while I have the time.
reactions.questionForOwner: Can I get the sandwich wrapped to take away if I'm running short on time?
reactions.diary: Ordered the €9.90 deal Tuesday at 12:30: short queue, food ready. Worth repeating if it stays quick.

reactions.thought: It's packed, so no room for a pram, and I still remember that reheated quiche. The new place two doors down does lunch for €8.50 and I've got no bad memory of it, so I'll try that.
reactions.questionForOwner: Do the soup and sandwiches in the deal contain nuts, and is the soup made fresh that day?
reactions.diary: Wed of week two: Lindenblatt was packed with no room for the pram, so I tried the new €8.50 place two doors down.

reactions.thought: Same as last week: no deciding, and it's cheaper than my usual €12.20. The new place two doors down is €8.50, but I don't know it and my break is short, so I stay with what I know.
reactions.questionForOwner: Will the deal stay at €9.90, and does the soup change during the week?
reactions.diary: Second week, Wednesday: took the €9.90 deal again; the €8.50 place two doors down didn't tempt me yet.

reactions.thought: The new place two doors down has an €8.50 lunch, €1.40 less than Lindenblatt's deal and closer to my budget. I'll try it, or go to the döner if it looks pricey.
reactions.questionForOwner: Could you do a smaller soup-and-drink deal for around €8?
reactions.diary: Week 2: skipped Lindenblatt's €9.90 deal for the new café's €8.50 lunch two doors down; still watching prices.

reactions.thought: The deal beat my usual by 30 cents and I get soup too. The new place's €8.50 is cheaper, but I know the staff here and it's busy for a reason. I'll take the deal again.
reactions.questionForOwner: Does mint tea count as the drink in the deal, and how long will it run?
reactions.diary: Week 2 Wednesday: took the €9.90 deal again; noted the new café's €8.50 but I stay for the staff.

reactions.thought: Still €9.90 on the board, still over my €7.20. The new place two doors down is €8.50, closer but still too much for me, and this one looks packed. Mensa it is.
reactions.questionForOwner: Do you ever do a soup-only or half-sandwich option for around €6-7?
reactions.diary: Week two, board still €9.90 and the new café is €8.50; Mensa won again, only a €6-7 soup or half-sandwich deal would get me in.

reactions.thought: Busy at 12:45, but I have a window before pick-up and the deal was quick last time. The cheaper place two doors down is tempting, but I'll give this one another go.
reactions.questionForOwner: Can I order the deal ahead on WhatsApp or Instagram so it's ready when I get there? I only have a short window.
reactions.diary: Second visit for the €9.90 deal, Wednesday 12:45: busy but I came back; a cheaper €8.50 place opened nearby, so speed decides it.

reactions.thought: I read the note walking past with the pram. Last time there was no room for the pram, and the place two doors down is cheaper at €8.50. I'm not going to fight for a table here.
reactions.questionForOwner: Are the soup and sandwich nut-free, and is there ever a quieter time with room for a pram?
reactions.diary: Friday of week two: read the 'tell us' note under the board, but kept going to the cheaper place two doors down.

reactions.thought: It's Friday, 12:30, and the deal is still the easiest choice. It costs less than my usual €12.20 and I don't have to decide. The €8.50 place hasn't pulled me away. I'd just keep taking it.
reactions.questionForOwner: Is the deal staying after the test, and will the soup or sandwich change, or is it always the same?
reactions.diary: End of the test, Friday: took the €9.90 deal again and hope they keep it, because it spares me deciding.

reactions.thought: I saw the note on my way past. The deal is still €9.90, which is €2 over what I spend and more than the new place's €8.50 lunch. I'm eating there again. Not worth writing a review.
reactions.questionForOwner: Would you ever do a soup and flat white combo for around €7.50? That's what I actually buy.
reactions.diary: End of test: ate at the cheaper café two doors down again; Lindenblatt's €9.90 deal stays out of my budget.

reactions.thought: I'm here anyway on a Friday and €9.90 for soup, sandwich and a drink beats my usual €10.20. The new place is cheaper, but I stay for the staff. I hope they keep the deal.
reactions.questionForOwner: Are you keeping the €9.90 deal after the test, and will it stay on weekdays?
reactions.diary: End of test Friday: took the €9.90 deal again; hoping they keep it, still choosing Lindenblatt over the €8.50 place for the staff.

reactions.thought: Saw the note, but the deal is still €9.90 and my lunch budget is €7.20. The Mensa is cheaper and the new café is €8.50. I'm not going to write a review for a place I've never eaten in.
reactions.questionForOwner: Would you ever do a smaller soup or half-sandwich lunch for €6-7?
reactions.diary: Two weeks on, the Lindenblatt deal is still €9.90, so the Mensa wins; I'd only come in for a €6-7 option.

reactions.thought: Third time I'm in for the deal. It's fair at €9.90 and it's ready fast, which matters on my lunch break. The €8.50 place is cheaper, but I'd rather save the 1.40 than lose time. I won't write anything.
reactions.questionForOwner: Will you keep the lunch deal, and can you keep it quick when it's busy? That's the only reason I'd pick it over the cheaper place.
reactions.diary: Friday after the test: back for the €9.90 deal a third time; I stay as long as it's fast and doesn't cost more.

interviews.question: What would make you come back for the lunch deal next week?

answers.name: Noor
answers.answer: Room for the pram, mainly. If I could count on a spot without a fight, and the board said what's in it and whether it has nuts, I'd try it. At €9.90 I'd still compare to the €8.50 place, though. Honestly I'm not sure a deal alone would do it.

answers.name: Chiara
answers.answer: Just keep it as it is: same price, same soup-sandwich-drink, available by 12:30 on weekdays. It saves me deciding on a short break and costs less than my usual lunch. The €8.50 place doesn't tempt me. If it disappears, I'd be back to my lunchbox or the bakery.

answers.name: Paweł
answers.answer: Honestly, a soup-and-drink option around €8, no sandwich needed. At €9.90 I'm paying €2 more for food I don't want, and the place two doors down is €8.50. Maybe on a good invoice week, but probably not next week.

answers.name: Murat
answers.answer: Honestly, I'd come anyway if the deal is still there at €9.90 and the sandwich isn't smaller. I'm in most days and I like the staff. If it went above my usual €10.20, I'd just go back to my sandwich and mint tea.

answers.name: Greta
answers.answer: A cheaper option. If there was a soup or half-sandwich deal for €6-7, I'd come in. At €9.90 the Mensa wins every time, so I probably won't be back next week. Nothing else would really change my mind.

answers.name: Jan
answers.answer: Mainly that it stays fast. I'm between drop-off and pick-up, so soup and sandwich ready quickly is what counts. €9.90 is fair; I'd stay if it doesn't cost more. The €8.50 place is cheaper, but I'd rather save time than 1.40.
